newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa buying weak amid futures upmove.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa buying weak amid futures upmove.

text.p: German chocolate manufacturers restricted themselves to replacement buying of cocoa as higher futures and a strong pound raised mark prices, traders said on Wednesday.
"Cocoa physicals are sluggish -- we've sold some spot butter and beans but distant dates are neglected," said one.
He said the March premium over December, at 39 stg at 1630 GMT, also encouraged the nearby purchases.
The London March contract traded three stg above last night at 940 stg, far from Nov 19's eight-month low of 903 stg, but below overhead resistance at 944 stg.
Elsewhere, the French truck strike brought some rejigging of transport schedules.

Liquid butter cargoes from the Netherland could not enter the country and had to be marketed elsewhere, traders said. But French cocoa products could not get out of the country and this meant processors in neighbouring countries were able to pick up third country business.
Selective strikes in German confectionery plants over sick pay, which on Wednesday involved 4,800 employees, were not yet seen as a threat to processing schedules.
"Some companies stepped up production ahead of the widely-publicised strike action and too few key plants are hit to cause any trouble," one trader said.
"But if it carried on for a long time, it could block butter transports and hamper new ordering."
Traders said the pace of cocoa arrivals in West Africa appeared to be slow.
They had heard rain was delaying transports to ports and causing mould and the final crop figure was also still unknown.
Local bean prices were at 2.27 marks/kg for 1996, up from 2.20-2.24 marks last week and 2.12 during futures lows earlier this month when processors last bought large volumes.
First quarter 1997 beans were at 2.32 marks.
The cocoa butter ratio was unchanged at 2.80 for 1996 dates and 2.70 for first quarter 1997.
Sterling was fixed in Frankfurt on Wednesday at 2.5558 marks compared with 2.5090 marks a week ago. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
